value: most sensitive at 3.2 kHz, with in-air thresholds of 13 and 14 dB re 20 uPa in the two sea lions
method: behavioural go/no-go audiometry, tone level lowered in 6 dB steps (staircase) until the animal stopped responding, in a soundproofed room with an anechoic chamber built inside it at Taronga Zoo, Sydney
conditions: two adult females, Nala (zoo-born, 17 years old) and Tarni (wild-born, 10 years old); tone frequencies 100 Hz to 20 kHz, each frequency tested in three sessions with the lowest threshold reported; the two audiograms were similar at 800 to 3200 Hz, and Tarni was less sensitive than Nala at lower and higher frequencies (Table 1 gives 72 vs 85 dB at 100 Hz and 27 vs 51 dB at 20 kHz, which animal is which not read); Tarni's 20 dB bandwidth of best sensitivity ran from about 600 Hz to 9 kHz and Nala's reached at least 20 kHz, the top of the tested range (tones above 20 kHz could not be projected), so her upper limit is not measured; which animal had 13 and which 14 dB is not stated in the quote
